card.name: Formal old-style prose, mid-sentence
card.fires_on: Words in archaic or formal historical prose, such as numbered ordinals (1st, 2d, 5th) in lists of conclusions or dates, and verbs or modifiers like have, could, will, without, last after a clause break.

modes.label: Ordinal numbers
modes.description: The digit before st, d or th in numbered conclusions or dates in old legal or scientific writing.
modes.example: we deduce the following conclusions; <<1>>st. That water is a binary compound

modes.label: Helper verbs in formal clauses
modes.description: Words like could, will, have, I that follow a name or clause in 19th-century historical prose.

modes.label: Emphatic quantity words
modes.description: Words such as one or last inside rhetorical oaths or vows.
modes.example: I would not hesitate<< one>> split second to enact legislation

card.writes: It leans away from emphatic adverbs like definitely and absolutely, so it does not push emphasis words.
card.plain: It fires on old, formal historical writing at points where the sentence is still unfolding, such as numbered points and helper verbs.
